jobs.description:
Scientific Assistant – Biomedical Data Science & Spinal Cord Injury Research

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Biomedical Data Science Lab investigates data-driven solutions for healthcare applications with a focus on neurological conditions and systemic infections such as sepsis. At the core of our research is the collaboration across disciplines spanning expertise in medicine, biology, computer, and data science. We seek a motivated scientific assistant to join this growing team and contribute to interdisciplinary research partnerships.

Project background

The Biomedical Data Science Lab at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Scientific Assistant to support our data-intensive projects in biomedical imaging and clinical research. This position offers an excellent opportunity to work at the forefront of biomedical data science, contributing to key projects including data curation, image segmentation, and tool development for clinical research applications. The scientific assistant will support the Biomedical Data Science Team for a range of application projects, with a particular focus on our work in pediatric sepsis, lower back pain, and pediatric neurooncology.

Job description

We are looking for a Scientific Assistant with a strong background in statistics, machine learning, and biomedical data science to support our research using the European Multicenter Study about Spinal Cord Injury (EMSCI) and related SCI databases.

The position combines hands-on data analysis and scientific project support with the coordination of scientific activities within our research network. The successful candidate will work closely with researchers, clinicians, and international collaborators to analyse large-scale longitudinal SCI datasets and contribute to scientific publications and meetings.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Conduct statistical and machine-learning analyses using EMSCI and related SCI datasets.

• Develop and validate predictive models of neurological recovery and functional outcomes after SCI.

• Perform data preprocessing, quality control, harmonisation, feature engineering, and exploratory data analysis.

• Apply appropriate statistical methods, including regression, longitudinal data analysis, survival analysis, and machine-learning approaches.

• Develop reproducible analytical workflows in R and/or Python.

• Contribute to scientific publications, reports, presentations, and grant applications.

• Collaborate with clinicians, neuroscientists, statisticians, and data scientists across participating SCI centres.

• Support the organisation and coordination of scientific meetings, workshops, consortium meetings, and other research activities, including scheduling, preparation of agendas and materials, communication with participants, and follow-up.

• Assist with the coordination of ongoing collaborative projects and follow-up of scientific activities and deliverables.

Profile

• MSc or equivalent degree in statistics, biostatistics, data science, biomedical engineering, computer science, epidemiology, neuroscience, or a related discipline.

• Strong background in statistics and/or machine learning.

• Experience working with longitudinal and/or clinical datasets.

• Strong programming skills in R and/or Python.

• Experience with statistical modelling, data visualisation, and reproducible research.

• Familiarity with machine-learning methods such as random forests, gradient boosting, neural networks, or related approaches.

• Previous experience working with EMSCI data or other large SCI databases is highly desirable.

stampa

Il Biomedical Data Science Lab di ETH Zurich invita le applicazioni di un Assistente Scientifico a sostenere i nostri progetti ad alta intensità di dati nell'imaging biomedico e nella ricerca clinica. Questa posizione offre un'eccellente opportunità di lavorare in prima linea nella scienza dei dati biomedici, contribuendo a progetti chiave tra cui la cura dei dati, la segmentazione delle immagini e lo sviluppo degli strumenti per applicazioni di ricerca clinica. L'assistente scientifico sosterrà il Biomedical Data Science Team per una serie di progetti applicativi, con particolare attenzione al nostro lavoro in sepsi pediatrica, dolore alla schiena inferiore e neurooncologia pediatrica.

Descrizione del lavoro

Siamo alla ricerca di un Assistente Scientifico con un forte background in statistica, machine learning e scienze dei dati biomediche per supportare la nostra ricerca utilizzando lo Studio Multicenter Europeo sulle lesioni spinali (EMSCI) e le relative basi di dati SCI.

La posizione combina l'analisi dei dati e il supporto scientifico del progetto con il coordinamento delle attività scientifiche all'interno della nostra rete di ricerca. Il candidato di successo lavorerà a stretto contatto con ricercatori, medici e collaboratori internazionali per analizzare i dataset SCI longitudinali su larga scala e contribuire a pubblicazioni e incontri scientifici.

Le tue responsabilità chiave includono:

• Contribuire a pubblicazioni scientifiche, relazioni, presentazioni e domande di sovvenzione.

The Biomedical Data Science Lab investigates data-driven solutions for healthcare applications with a focus on neurological conditions and systemic infections such as sepsis. Project background

imprimer
Drucken

Le Biomedical Data Science Lab étudie des solutions basées sur les données pour les applications de soins de santé en mettant l'accent sur les affections neurologiques et les infections systémiques telles que la septicémie. Au cœur de notre recherche se trouve la collaboration entre disciplines couvrant l'expertise en médecine, en biologie, en informatique et en sciences des données. Nous cherchons un assistant scientifique motivé pour rejoindre cette équipe croissante et contribuer à des partenariats de recherche interdisciplinaires.

Contexte du projet

Le laboratoire de données biomédicales de l'ETH Zurich invite des applications pour un assistant scientifique afin de soutenir nos projets à forte intensité de données en imagerie biomédicale et en recherche clinique. Ce poste offre une excellente occasion de travailler à l'avant-garde de la science des données biomédicales, contribuant à des projets clés tels que la curation des données, la segmentation des images et le développement d'outils pour les applications de recherche clinique. L'assistant scientifique appuiera l'équipe des données biomédicales pour toute une gamme de projets d'application, en mettant particulièrement l'accent sur nos travaux en septicémie pédiatrique, en douleur lombaire et en neurooncologie pédiatrique.

Description du poste

Nous sommes à la recherche d'un assistant scientifique ayant une solide expérience en statistique, en apprentissage automatique et en science des données biomédicales pour soutenir notre recherche à l'aide de l'Étude multicentrique européenne sur les lésions de la moelle épinière (EMSCI) et des bases de données SCI connexes.

Le poste combine l'analyse de données pratiques et le soutien de projets scientifiques avec la coordination des activités scientifiques au sein de notre réseau de recherche. Le candidat retenu travaillera en étroite collaboration avec des chercheurs, des cliniciens et des collaborateurs internationaux pour analyser les ensembles de données longitudinales à grande échelle de l'ICS et contribuer aux publications et réunions scientifiques.

Vos principales responsabilités comprendront :

• Effectuer des analyses statistiques et de l'apprentissage automatique à l'aide de l'EMSCI et des ensembles de données SCI connexes.

• Élaborer et valider des modèles prédictifs de récupération neurologique et de résultats fonctionnels après SCI.

• Effectuer le prétraitement des données, le contrôle de la qualité, l'harmonisation, l'ingénierie des caractéristiques et l'analyse des données exploratoires.

• Appliquer des méthodes statistiques appropriées, y compris la régression, l'analyse des données longitudinales, l'analyse de la survie et les approches d'apprentissage automatique.

• Élaborer des flux de travail analytiques reproductibles en R et/ou en Python.

• Contribuer aux publications scientifiques, rapports, présentations et demandes de subvention.

• Collaborer avec les cliniciens, les neuroscientifiques, les statisticiens et les spécialistes des données dans les centres SCI participants.

• Appuyer l'organisation et la coordination de réunions scientifiques, d'ateliers, de réunions de consortiums et d'autres activités de recherche, y compris l'établissement de calendriers, la préparation d'ordres du jour et de documents, la communication avec les participants et le suivi.

• Aider à la coordination des projets de collaboration en cours et au suivi des activités et des résultats scientifiques.

Profil

• Maîtrise en statistique, biostatistique, sciences des données, génie biomédical, informatique, épidémiologie, neurosciences ou discipline connexe.

• Forte expérience en statistique et/ou en apprentissage automatique.

• Expérience de travail avec des ensembles de données longitudinales et/ou cliniques.

• Fortes compétences en programmation en R et/ou Python.

• Expérience en modélisation statistique, visualisation des données et recherche reproductible.

• Familiarisation avec les méthodes d'apprentissage automatique telles que les forêts aléatoires, l'augmentation des gradients, les réseaux neuronaux ou les approches connexes.

• Une expérience antérieure de travail avec des données EMSCI ou d'autres grandes bases de données SCI est hautement souhaitable.

• La connaissance des mesures des résultats cliniques et neurologiques propres aux ISC (p. ex. ISNCSCI/ASIA, SCIM) est un avantage.

• L'expérience de travail avec des ensembles de données cliniques multicentriques est un avantage.

• Habile en anglais et compétent en allemand, à la fois écrit et parlé.

• Excellentes compétences en matière d'organisation et de communication.

40%-50%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Am Departement Biologie (D-BIOL) der ETH Zürich ist für den Studiengang Lehrdiplom für Maturitätsschulen auf Herbstsemester 2027 die Position als Fachdidaktiker:in Biologie zu besetzen (Stellenbeginn: 01.08.2027).

Biologie ist eine Schlüsselwissenschaft des 21. Jahrhunderts. Unseren Gymnasiast:innen soll ein solides Grundverständnis biologischer Prozesse vermittelt werden, damit sie sich in Diskussionen zu aktuellen Themen wie dem Rückgang der Biodiversität, den Auswirkungen der globalen Erwärmung, modernen Reproduktionstechnologien und gentechnisch veränderten Organismen einbringen können. Die ETH engagiert sich für eine zeitgemässe Ausbildung von Lehrpersonen, die dieser anspruchsvollen Aufgabe gewachsen sind.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Sie sind verantwortlich für die Gestaltung und Durchführung der Lehrveranstaltungen in der Fachdidaktik Biologie.

• Sie beraten Studierende, rekrutieren und betreuen Praktikumslehrpersonen, teilen Studierenden Plätze für Unterrichtspraktika zu, helfen bei der Betreuung von mentorierten Arbeiten und nehmen Prüfungslektionen ab.

Profil

• Sie verfügen über einen universitären Hochschulabschluss in Biologie (oder einer nahe verwandten Disziplin) sowie über das Lehrdiplom für Maturitätsschulen (oder einen äquivalenten didaktischen Abschluss).

• Sie bringen mehrjährige Unterrichtserfahrung an einem Gymnasium in der Schweiz mit.

• Sie unterrichten zur Zeit an einem Gymnasium .

• Sie zeichnen sich durch ausgewiesene Kompetenzen in der Gestaltung lernwirksamen Unterrichts aus und sind mit Konzepten der fachdidaktischen Forschung vertraut. In Ihrer Lehrpraxis wenden Sie verschiedene aktivierende Unterrichtsmethoden an und entwickeln diese ständig weiter.

• Von Vorteil ist Erfahrung mit Studierenden, beispielsweise als Praktikumslehrperson.

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

In der Didaktischen Ausbildung der ETH Zürich erwartet Sie ein interdisziplinäres Team von Lehr-/Lernforschenden, Fachdidaktiker:innen verschiedener Fächer sowie Praktikumslehrpersonen und Fachwissenschaftler:innen Ihres Faches. Sie erhalten Fort- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten sowohl im didaktisch-pädagogischen Bereich als auch fachwissenschaftlich am D-BIOL.

chevron_right

Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden. Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent an einer klimaneutralen Zukunft.

Neugierig? Sind wir auch.

jobs.description:
Doctoral Positions in Robot Learning and Soft, Musculoskeletal, and Biohybrid Robotics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for several doctoral positions. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. We work along four directions: soft and musculoskeletal robotics, biohybrid living systems, dexterous manipulation and robot learning, and simulation for embodied AI. We are looking for exceptional candidates in any of them. This round we especially want two profiles: people who design and build the robots, and people who make policies run on them.

We do not hire against a narrow project description. Your thesis topic is something we shape together in your first months. Tell us which of our directions pulls at you, and what you would want to build.

Project background

Today's robots are mostly rigid, fragile, and a world apart from the agility and resilience of biological bodies. Our bet is that the next generation of robots will be soft, musculoskeletal, and in part alive. They will be built to make contact with the real world rather than to avoid it. We pursue this across four directions, and a strong candidate will find a home in one of them and borrow from the others.

Soft and musculoskeletal robotics. We build bodies from compliant structures, bones, joints, and tendon-like actuation. Our electrohydraulic musculoskeletal leg jumps, moves fast, and adapts to terrain at roughly 1.2% of the energy a motor-driven leg needs ( Nature Communications, 2024 ). Our low-voltage HASEL actuators run near 1100 V, are safe to touch, and work untethered and underwater ( Science Advances, 2024 ). We recently extended these muscles to full antagonistic motion ranges ( ICRA 2025 ) and to a sensorless, inherently compliant anthropomorphic hand driven entirely by electrohydraulic actuation ( IROS 2026 ).

Biohybrid living systems. We grow engineered muscle and use it to actuate machines. We bioprinted multicellular muscle-tendon units that transmit force along a real musculoskeletal path ( Science Advances, 2025 ), embedded sensors directly into muscle for closed-loop control of proprioceptive biohybrid robots ( Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025 ), and established functional volumetric bioprinting with xolography ( Advanced Materials, 2026 ). Co-optimized volumetric muscle designs for large dynamic deformations are in press at Nature Communications (Balciunaite et al., 2026). The same fabrication line reaches clinical work: with University Hospital Zurich we printed implantable reinforced cardiac tissue patches ( Advanced Materials, 2025 ).

Dexterous manipulation and robot learning. We build hands and the policies that run them. One of our initial hand designs is now commercialized through our spin-off Mimic Robotics . ORCA is our open-source, reliable, and cost-effective anthropomorphic hand for uninterrupted dexterous task learning ( IROS 2025 ). On that hardware we work on imitation learning and diffusion policies, cross-embodiment skill transfer through latent action diffusion (ICRA 2026), sample-efficient reinforcement learning and policy fine-tuning directly on the real robot , vision-language-action models for contact-rich tasks, and tactile representation learning on our high-resolution sensorized skin (ICRA 2024). We also build controllable dexterous world models for training and evaluation, and a benchmark of dexterity for anthropomorphic hands . Whichever side you come from, the offer is the same: the hand, the skin, the simulator, and the people who designed all three sit in one room. Build a mechanism here and someone will have a policy running on it within weeks. Build a policy here and you can change the mechanism when the mechanism is what is wrong.

Simulation, fabrica

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in neutral-atom quantum computing

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The newly established Atom Quantum Processing (AQP) group , led by Prof. Konrad Viebahn, at the Institute for Quantum Electronics within the Physics Department (D-PHYS), ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated Doctoral Candidate.

Our research focusses on ultracold neutral atoms and their application in quantum technologies, in particular, quantum computing. We are currently establishing a new laboratory for laser cooling, trapping, and imaging ultracold rubidium atoms in optical lattices. With newly developed methods, such as high-fidelity collisional atom-atom interactions, we build highly coherent quantum machines capable of creating massively entangled quantum states for computing, simulation, sensing, and metrology.

Project background

Neutral atoms are one of the most promising quantum architectures of today. Yet, the current roadmaps towards neutral-atom fault-tolerant quantum computers are almost exclusively based on Rydberg interactions in optical tweezers. While Rydberg-based gates are fast, they have a massive drawback: finite Rydberg lifetimes and unavoidable decoherence due to spontaneous emission. Instead, our research will employ collisional interactions between atomic qubits, which are highly coherent, passively stable, and very scalable. By using optical lattices instead of optical tweezers we can trap and control more qubits per given laser power, eventually leading to a scalability advantage over the neutral-atom state-of-the-art.

We have recently overcome an important bottleneck in optical-lattice-based quantum processors, by integrating topological pumping as a method to shuttle atoms between lattice sites (see publications ). When combined with stable collisional gates, a new quantum architecture emerges with the ability to create massively entangled states, large-scale quantum simulation, quantum sensing and, eventually, fault-tolerant computing.

In this experimental Doctoral project, you will play a central role in setting up the experimental apparatus, building a closely-knit team, and developing new concepts in collisional quantum processing.

Job description

• Building up the AQP team in a collaborative, enthusiastic, and communicative environment

• Setting up laser system for laser cooling, trapping, and imaging of rubidium-85 atoms

• Engineering and assembling UHV (ultra-high vacuum) system with excellent optical access for the quantum processor

• Programming and integrating experimental control hardware (ARTIQ) for running quantum information experiments

• Investigating novel schemes for quantum information processing based on collisional interactions, including theoretical calculations and numerical simulations

• Preseting your results at scientific conferences and publishing your work

Profile

• You should hold (or be close to completing) an MSc degree in physics, quantum engineering, electrical engineering, or closely related discipline

• You should have a strong motivation to build a quantum computer from scratch

• Excellent spoken and written English

• Willingness to work in an international and diverse team

Experience in any of the following laboratory techniques would be advantageous:

• Fibre coupling

• Optical/fluorescence microscopy

• Doppler-free absorption spectroscopy

• Spatial light modulation

• Laser locking, optical resonators

• Optical interferometers

• Gaussian beam profiling

• CAD development

• Soldering

• PCB development

• FPGA development

• Digital signal processing (DSP)

Workplace

We offer

We offer a stimulating doctoral project on quantum computing with state-of-the-art neutral-atom techniques. The successful candidate with join a collaborative and international research group and will receive training in experimental techniques for AMO and quantum optics. Druppo

Il nuovo gruppo Atom Quantum Processing (AQP), guidato dal Prof. Konrad Viebahn, presso l'Istituto di Elettronica Quantica all'interno del Dipartimento di Fisica (D-PHYS), ETH Zurich, sta cercando un Dottorato altamente motivato.

La nostra ricerca si concentra sugli atomi neutri ultrafreddi e sulla loro applicazione nelle tecnologie quantistiche, in particolare nell'informatica quantistica. Attualmente stiamo creando un nuovo laboratorio per il raffreddamento laser, il trapping e l'imaging atomi di rubidio ultrafreddi in reticoli ottici. Con nuovi metodi, come le interazioni atom-atom collisionali ad alta fedeltà, costruiamo macchine quantistiche altamente coerenti in grado di creare stati quantici massicciamente impigliati per l'elaborazione, la simulazione, il rilevamento e la metrologia.

Sfondo del progetto

Gli atomi neutri sono una delle architetture quantistiche più promettenti di oggi. Tuttavia, le attuali roadmap verso i computer quantici neutral-atom-tolleranti sono quasi esclusivamente basate sulle interazioni Rydberg in pinzette ottiche. Mentre i cancelli a base di Rydberg sono veloci, hanno un enorme inconveniente: finite vite di Rydberg e decoherence inevitabile a causa di emissione spontanea. Invece, la nostra ricerca utilizzerà interazioni collisionali tra qubit atomici, che sono altamente coerenti, passivamente stabili e molto scalabili. Utilizzando reticoli ottici invece di pinzette ottiche possiamo intrappolare e controllare più qubit per data potenza laser, alla fine portando a un vantaggio di scalabilità sullo stato dell'arte neutro-atomo.

Abbiamo recentemente superato un importante collo di bottiglia in processori quantici basati su reticolo ottico, integrando la pompazione topologica come metodo per trasportare gli atomi tra siti reticoli (vedi pubblicazioni). Quando combinato con cancelli collisionali stabili, una nuova architettura quantistica emerge con la capacità di creare stati massicciamente impigliati, simulazione quantistica su larga scala, rilevamento quantico e, infine, elaborazione di errore tollerante.

In questo progetto sperimentale di Doctoral, si svolgerà un ruolo centrale nella creazione dell'apparato sperimentale, la costruzione di un team strettamente legato, e lo sviluppo di nuovi concetti nella elaborazione quantistica collisionale.

• Ottimo parlato e scritto inglese

• Volontà di lavorare in un team internazionale e diversificato

Druck

Die neu gegründete Gruppe Atom Quantum Processing (AQP) unter der Leitung von Prof. Konrad Viebahn am Institut für Quantenelektronik der Physikabteilung (D-PHYS), ETH Zürich, sucht einen hochmotivierten Doktoranden.

Unsere Forschung konzentriert sich auf ultrakalte neutrale Atome und ihre Anwendung in Quantentechnologien, insbesondere im Quantencomputing. Derzeit bauen wir ein neues Labor für Laserkühlung, Einfangen und Bildgebung ultrakalter Rubidiumatome in optischen Gittern auf. Mit neu entwickelten Methoden, wie hochgenauen kollisiven Atom-Atom-Wechselwirkungen, bauen wir hochkohärente Quantenmaschinen, die massiv verschränkte Quantenzustände für Computer, Simulation, Sensorik und Metrologie erzeugen können.

Projekthintergrund

Neutrale Atome sind eine der vielversprechendsten Quantenarchitekturen von heute. Die aktuellen Roadmaps für neutral-atomfehlertolerante Quantencomputer basieren jedoch fast ausschließlich auf Rydberg-Wechselwirkungen in optischen Pinzetten. Während Rydberg-basierte Tore schnell sind, haben sie einen massiven Nachteil: endliche Rydberg-Lebenszeiten und unvermeidliche Dekohärenz durch spontane Emission. Stattdessen wird unsere Forschung Kollisionswechselwirkungen zwischen atomaren Qubits einsetzen, die sehr kohärent, passiv stabil und sehr skalierbar sind. Durch die Verwendung von optischen Gittern anstelle von optischen Pinzetten können wir mehr Qubits pro gegebener Laserleistung einfangen und steuern, was schließlich zu einem Skalierbarkeitsvorteil gegenüber dem Stand der Technik führt.

Wir haben kürzlich einen wichtigen Engpass bei optischen gitterbasierten Quantenprozessoren überwunden, indem wir topologisches Pumpen als eine Methode zum Shuttlen von Atomen zwischen Gitterstellen integriert haben (siehe Publikationen ). In Kombination mit stabilen Kollisionstoren entsteht eine neue Quantenarchitektur mit der Fähigkeit, massiv verschränkte Zustände, groß angelegte Quantensimulation, Quantensensorik und schließlich fehlertolerantes Rechnen zu erzeugen.

In diesem experimentellen Doktorandenprojekt spielen Sie eine zentrale Rolle beim Aufbau des experimentellen Apparats, beim Aufbau eines engmaschigen Teams und bei der Entwicklung neuer Konzepte in der kollisiven Quantenverarbeitung.

Le groupe Atom Quantum Processing (AQP) nouvellement créé, dirigé par le professeur Konrad Viebahn, à l'Institut d'électronique quantique au sein du Département de physique (D-PHYS), ETH Zurich, cherche un candidat doctorant hautement motivé.

Notre recherche se concentre sur les atomes neutres ultrafroids et leur application dans les technologies quantiques, en particulier le calcul quantique. Nous sommes en train de créer un nouveau laboratoire pour le refroidissement laser, le piégeage et l'imagerie des atomes de rubidium ultrafroids dans les réseaux optiques. Avec des méthodes nouvellement développées, comme les interactions atom-atome collisionnelle à haute fidélité, nous construisons des machines quantiques hautement cohérentes capables de créer des états quantiques massivement enchevêtrés pour l'informatique, la simulation, la détection et la métrologie.

Contexte du projet

Les atomes neutres sont l'une des architectures quantiques les plus prometteuses d'aujourd'hui. Pourtant, les feuilles de route actuelles vers des ordinateurs quantiques neutres et tolérants aux défauts sont presque exclusivement basées sur les interactions Rydberg dans les pinces optiques. Tandis que les portes basées sur Rydberg sont rapides, elles présentent un inconvénient énorme : les durées de vie finies de Rydberg et la décohérence inévitable due à une émission spontanée. Notre recherche utilisera plutôt des interactions collisionnelles entre qubits atomiques, qui sont très cohérents, passivement stables et très évolutives. En utilisant des treillis optiques au lieu de pinces optiques, nous pouvons piéger et contrôler plus de qubits par puissance laser donnée, menant finalement à un avantage d'évolutivité par rapport à l'état de l'atome neutre.

Nous avons récemment surmonté un important goulot d'étranglement dans les processeurs quantiques à base de réseaux optiques, en intégrant le pompage topologique comme méthode de navette des atomes entre les sites de réseaux (voir publications ). Combiné à des portes de collision stables, une nouvelle architecture quantique émerge avec la capacité de créer des états fortement enchevêtrés, la simulation quantique à grande échelle, la détection quantique et, éventuellement, l'informatique tolérante aux défauts.

Dans ce projet expérimental de Doctorat, vous jouerez un rôle central dans la mise en place de l'appareil expérimental, la construction d'une équipe de près et le développement de nouveaux concepts dans le traitement quantique collisionnel.

• Programmation et intégration du matériel de commande expérimental (ARTIQ) pour des expériences d'information quantique

• Étude de nouveaux schémas de traitement de l'information quantique basés sur des interactions collisionnelles, y compris des calculs théoriques et des simulations numériques

• Préréglage de vos résultats lors de conférences scientifiques et publication de vos travaux

Profil

• Vous devriez détenir (ou être près de terminer) un diplôme de maîtrise en physique, génie quantique, génie électrique ou discipline étroitement liée

• Vous devriez avoir une forte motivation pour construire un ordinateur quantique à partir de zéro

• Excellent anglais parlé et écrit

Postdoctoral Positions in Robot Learning and Soft, Musculoskeletal, and Biohybrid Robotics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Soft Robotics Lab within the Institute of Robotics and Intelligent Systems at ETH Zurich is inviting applications for several open postdoctoral positions. Our lab's goal is to build, model, and control robots in a fundamentally different way, so that they become more flexible, dexterous, capable, and adapt better to their environment. We work along four directions: soft and musculoskeletal robotics, biohybrid living systems, dexterous manipulation and robot learning, and simulation for embodied AI. We are looking for exceptional candidates in any of them. This round we especially want two profiles: people who design and build the robots, and people who make policies run on them.

We do not hire against a narrow project description. We hire people who will define their own. Tell us which of our directions you want to push, and why you are the person to push it.

Project background

Today's robots are mostly rigid, fragile, and a world apart from the agility and resilience of biological bodies. Our bet is that the next generation of robots will be soft, musculoskeletal, and in part alive. They will be built to make contact with the real world rather than to avoid it. We pursue this across four directions, and a strong candidate will find a home in one of them and borrow from the others.

Soft and musculoskeletal robotics. We build bodies from compliant structures, bones, joints, and tendon-like actuation. Our electrohydraulic musculoskeletal leg jumps, moves fast, and adapts to terrain at roughly 1.2% of the energy a motor-driven leg needs ( Nature Communications, 2024 ). Our low-voltage HASEL actuators run near 1100 V, are safe to touch, and work untethered and underwater ( Science Advances, 2024 ). We recently extended these muscles to full antagonistic motion ranges ( ICRA 2025 ) and to a sensorless, inherently compliant anthropomorphic hand driven entirely by electrohydraulic actuation ( IROS 2026 ).

Biohybrid living systems. We grow engineered muscle and use it to actuate machines. We bioprinted multicellular muscle-tendon units that transmit force along a real musculoskeletal path ( Science Advances, 2025 ), embedded sensors directly into muscle for closed-loop control of proprioceptive biohybrid robots ( Advanced Intelligent Systems, 2025 ), and established functional volumetric bioprinting with xolography ( Advanced Materials, 2026 ). Co-optimized volumetric muscle designs for large dynamic deformations are in press at Nature Communications (Balciunaite et al., 2026). The same fabrication line reaches clinical work: with University Hospital Zurich we printed implantable reinforced cardiac tissue patches ( Advanced Materials, 2025 ).

Dexterous manipulation and robot learning. We build hands and the policies that run them. One of our initial hand designs is now commercialized through our spin-off Mimic Robotics . ORCA is our open-source, reliable, and cost-effective anthropomorphic hand for uninterrupted dexterous task learning ( IROS 2025 ). On that hardware we work on imitation learning and diffusion policies, cross-embodiment skill transfer through latent action diffusion (ICRA 2026), sample-efficient reinforcement learning and policy fine-tuning directly on the real robot , vision-language-action models for contact-rich tasks, and tactile representation learning on our high-resolution sensorized skin (ICRA 2024). We also build controllable dexterous world models for training and evaluation, and a benchmark of dexterity for anthropomorphic hands . Whichever side you come from, the offer is the same: the hand, the skin, the simulator, and the people who designed all three sit in one room. Student Assistant for Prenatal Genetics Project

10%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Health Ethics & Policy Lab is conducting a SNSF-funded project on the ethics of prenatal genetic testing . As part of this project, we are conducting interview studies with pregnant patients and families with a rare disease diagnosis to understand their views and experiences with prenatal genetic testing.

Le Health Ethics & Policy Lab mène un projet financé par la SNSF sur l'éthique des tests génétiques prénatals. Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous menons des études d'entrevue avec des patientes enceintes et des familles ayant un diagnostic de maladie rare afin de comprendre leur point de vue et leurs expériences en matière de dépistage génétique prénatal.

Description du poste

Nous sommes à la recherche d'un assistant de recherche avec compétence en français, en italien et en anglais pour mener et traiter des entrevues avec les participants à l'étude au cours de l'année académique 2026-2027 (principalement au cours du semestre d'automne, bien qu'il puisse y avoir encore du travail au début du semestre du printemps). Notre laboratoire fournira la formation nécessaire pour réussir dans ce poste, bien que l'expérience antérieure de l'entrevue semi-structurée soit un atout.

Les tâches peuvent comprendre :

• Vérification de l'exactitude et nettoyage des données des transcriptions des entrevues dans la langue dans laquelle elles sont effectuées.

Profil

Requis

• Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite en français et/ou en italien (C1+, de préférence langue maternelle). La préférence sera donnée aux candidats qui parlent couramment les deux langues.

• Fortes compétences en communication orale et écrite en anglais (B2+).

• Capacité de discuter de sujets sensibles de manière bienveillante et empathique.

• Capacité de travailler de façon indépendante, fiable et précise.

Désireux

• Expérience préalable ou connaissance des entrevues et des méthodologies qualitatives.

• Intérêt pour la bioéthique, y compris la génétique et l'éthique reproductive.

Lieu de travail

Nous offrons

Il s'agit d'un poste horaire, et le salaire sera basé sur les heures de travail accomplies. Le travail hybride est possible et les temps de travail flexibles. Ce poste offrira une expérience de recherche précieuse et l'occasion d'en apprendre davantage sur le domaine de la bioéthique. Vous travaillerez principalement avec un doctorant et le co-PI du projet. Si vous êtes intéressé par d'autres aspects du travail dans notre laboratoire, vous serez invités à assister à diverses présentations et clubs de revues.

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in solid-state transformer development, with a focus on high-power medium-frequency transformers

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on Solid-State-Transformers for future PV and energy storage systems, we are looking for a: Doctoral Position for developing solid state transformers with the focus on high-power medium frequency transformers.

Job description

• Doctoral research on modelling and optimisation of high-power Solid-State Transformers (SSTs), focusing on Medium-Frequency Transformers (MFTs).

• Investigation of high-frequency and high-voltage MFTs for PV systems and medium-voltage grids.

• Integration of battery storage systems and control of dynamic power flow between batteries and the grid.

• Development of multiphysics models for losses, temperature, cooling, resonances and electrical insulation.

• Optimisation of core, windings and cooling for improved efficiency, power density and power transfer.

• Development and optimisation of SST systems and power electronic converters.

• Integration of models into computationally efficient optimisation procedures and collaboration with other Doctoral Position.

• Design, construction and experimental validation of MFT prototypes and converter systems.

Profile

• A diploma/M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering with excellent grades.

• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems.

• Good communication skills.

• Fluency in English.

• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.

• In addition, you should be interested in the detailed modelling and design of magnetic components and the optimisation of power electronic systems.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

• Our laboratory offers a challenging and scientifically highly exciting full-time position in a dynamic, international team at one of the world-wide leading technical universities

• We strongly encourage participation at international conferences and offer a competitive salary, excellent benefits as well as outstanding research and laboratory facilities for your experiments

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• Your B.S.

print

The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on Solid-State-Transformers for future PV and energy storage systems, we are looking for a: Doctoral Position for developing solid state transformers with the focus on high-power medium frequency transformers.

Job description

• Doctoral research on modelling and optimisation of high-power Solid-State Transformers (SSTs), focusing on Medium-Frequency Transformers (MFTs).

• Investigation of high-frequency and high-voltage MFTs for PV systems and medium-voltage grids.

• Integration of battery storage systems and control of dynamic power flow between batteries and the grid.

• Development of multiphysics models for losses, temperature, cooling, resonances and electrical insulation.

• Optimisation of core, windings and cooling for improved efficiency, power density and power transfer.

• Development and optimisation of SST systems and power electronic converters.

• Integration of models into computationally efficient optimisation procedures and collaboration with other Doctoral Position.

• Design, construction and experimental validation of MFT prototypes and converter systems.

jobs.description:
Fachspezialistin Studienadministration (m/w/d)

80%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

An der ETH Zürich studieren über 20'000 Studierende auf Bachelor- und Masterstufe oder sind als Hörerinnen und Hörer eingeschrieben. Die Abteilung Akademische Dienste schafft die administrativen Grundvoraussetzungen für die Lehre und verantwortet zentrale Prozesse des Lehrbetriebs für die gesamte ETH Zürich.

Der Bereich Studienadministration ist Teil der Akademischen Dienste und begleitet Studierende vor und während des Studiums in administrativen Belangen.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir per 1. Dezember 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte und zuverlässige Persönlichkeit als Fachspezialist:in Studienadministration. Die Stelle ist auf zwei Jahre befristet.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Sie sind Teil des Teams, welches sich um die Gesuche für Ausnahmeregelungen kümmert. Sie klären Sachverhalte sorgfältig ab, bearbeiten die Anträge und bereiten die entsprechenden Entscheidungsgrundlagen vor.

• Sie sind erste Anlaufstelle für Ihr Team und die Studienadministration bei Anfragen zu laufenden oder früheren Gesuchen– dabei behalten Sie auch bei komplexen Fällen den Überblick und sorgen für eine klare, verständliche Kommunikation.

• Sie pflegen die relevanten Daten in den entsprechenden Systemen und stellen sicher, dass Fristen zuverlässig eingehalten werden.

• Sie arbeiten zusammen mit den zuständigen Beratungsstellen, den Studienadministrationen der Studiengänge sowie weiteren Ansprechpersonen innerhalb der ETH Zürich.

• Zusätzlich unterstützen Sie die Leitung und das Leitungsteam der Studienadministration administrativ und organisatorisch. Bei der Organisation von Sitzungen und Anlässen übernehmen Sie die Planung, Koordination und Nachbereitung – von der Terminfindung über die Protokollführung bis hin zur Umsetzung vereinbarter Massnahmen.

• Sie wirken aktiv an der Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen und Abläufen mit, bringen eigene Ideen ein und tragen dazu bei, dass Gesuchsverfahren laufend optimiert werden.

Profil

• Sie verfügen über eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung auf Tertiärstufe (Uni, FH, HF oder ähnliches) und bringen idealerweise Erfahrung in der öffentlichen Verwaltung, im Hochschulumfeld oder in der Dossier-Bearbeitung mit.

• Sie arbeiten sehr sorgfältig, strukturiert und eigenständig.

• Sie gehen Aufgaben lösungsorientiert an.

• Sie gehen professionell mit sensiblen persönlichen und medizinischen Informationen um.

• Sie kommunizieren stilsicher, klar und adressatengerecht.

• Sie schätzen den Austausch im Team sowie die Zusammenarbeit mit verschiedenen Fachstellen innerhalb der ETH Zürich.

• Neben ausgezeichneten Deutschkenntnissen verfügen Sie über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse. Kenntnisse weiterer Landessprachen sind von Vorteil.

• Eine hohe IT-Affinität sowie die Fähigkeit, sich rasch in neue Applikationen und digitale Prozesse einzuarbeiten, runden Ihr Profil ab.

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit mit klarem Zuständigkeitsbereich, eingebettet in ein lebendiges Hochschulumfeld mit wechselnden und spannenden Herausforderungen.

• Einen Arbeitsplatz an einer der renommiertesten Hochschulen der Welt.

• Ein engagiertes und motiviertes Team.

• Attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen.

chevron_right

Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden. Postdoc in modelling of early prokaryote evolution and interaction with earth geodynamics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures), whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements, requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Details on NCCR Genesis are available on the website .

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. In the context of this project, we are looking for a 2-years fully funded postdoctoral candidate.

Project background

How did the earliest forms of life evolve, and how did their evolution interact with the changing physical and chemical environment of the early Earth? This project investigates the co-evolution of life and the Earth system over geological timescales, with a particular focus on the major transitions in energy metabolism of early prokaryotic life. The emergence and succession of different energy metabolisms was likely allowed by changing earth surface conditions. It is unclear which metabolic strategies were most likely to have emerged first, and how shifting environmental conditions may have determined major metabolic transitions in Earth’s history. The project will couple models of prokaryotic evolution and energy metabolism with existing and newly developed geodynamic simulations of the early Earth. These simulations will explore how mantle dynamics, lithospheric rheology, surface relief, weathering, CO₂ fluxes, palaeogeography, atmosphere, and climate evolved as the Earth cooled.

Beyond environmental triggers, the project aims to investigate the environmental transformation caused by these innovations. The evolution of organisms capable of autotrophic carbon fixation, for example, may have altered carbon and nutrient cycling, atmospheric composition, oxygen availability, and ultimately the conditions under which subsequent forms of life could evolve. Further attention will be given to how different geodynamic regimes may create environmental conditions that promote, delay, or prevent major evolutionary transitions. The project will explore a range of planetary and geodynamic scenarios, including early Earth conditions, or stagnant-lid. The resulting changes in tectonics, topography, surface processes, atmospheric composition, climate, and habitability will be linked to evolutionary models to determine when metabolic transitions are likely to occur. The project will contribute to understanding how planets and life co-evolve and how biological activity can fundamentally reshape planetary conditions.

Job description

As a postdoctoral researcher, you will develop and implement an interdisciplinary research programme investigating the evolution of early prokaryotic life in its geodynamic and climatic context. You will work at the interface of evolutionary biology, molecular evolution, geodynamics, Earth-system science, and planetary habitability.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Building up on existing modeling of anerobic autotrophs and heterotrophs (Sauterey et al 2020, Nasreldine et al in prep) to design a model simulating assemblages of metabolic communities as a function of glo

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Fellow / Process Engineer for metal assisted chemical etching

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The X-ray Imaging Professorship is dedicated to advancing the clinical translation of grating-based X-ray interferometry in close collaboration with industrial partners. This groundbreaking technology relies on the development of state-of-the-art X-ray optics enabled by cutting-edge micro- and nanofabrication techniques.

To support this effort, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher or Process Engineer to join the SNSF-funded project ABSOLUTE , working under the supervision of our micro- and nanofabrication specialist, Dr. Lucia Romano, at the Paul Scherrer Institute. As part of a multidisciplinary team of academic and industrial researchers, you will contribute to the development and optimization of next-generation fabrication technologies with direct relevance to advanced X-ray imaging applications.

The SNSF-funded project ABSOLUTE (n A noassem B led cataly S t and electr O chemica L processing for h U ge aspec T ratio microstructur E s) focuses on developing an innovative catalyst concept for defect control in metal-assisted chemical etching (MacEtch) of silicon. The project aims to overcome key challenges in the fabrication of high-aspect-ratio microstructures by improving process reliability, scalability, and manufacturing quality.

Job description

In this role, your primary responsibility will be to expand and enhance our MacEtch testing capabilities across a broad range of feature sizes and aspect ratios. You will investigate defect formation mechanisms, optimize process parameters, assess scalability, and contribute to the development of robust fabrication processes that enable the production of complex silicon microstructures for future X-ray optical components.

You will contribute to cutting-edge research in:

• Integration, qualification, and performance assessment of an advanced and unconventional microfabrication process

• Systematic optimization of fabrication parameters to improve process robustness, reproducibility, and scalability

• Characterization of high-aspect-ratio etched microstructures, including the development of dedicated metrology and defect-analysis methodologies

Your responsibilities

• Fabricate and process samples on 4-inch silicon wafers using UV photolithography, thin-film deposition, thermal treatments, and metal-assisted chemical etching (MacEtch)

• Perform structural and dimensional characterization using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and profilometry

• Document fabrication procedures, process results, and experimental findings in a structured and traceable manner

• Analyze data, prepare technical reports, and contribute to project deliverables

• Present research outcomes at international conferences, scientific symposia, and internal workshops

• Disseminate results through high-impact scientific publications and collaborative research activities

Profile

We are seeking a highly motivated professional with a strong collaborative mindset, a hands-on approach to problem solving, and a demonstrated ability to deliver results in a dynamic research environment.

• PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, Engineering, or a closely related discipline

• Proven experience working in semiconductor cleanroom environments, with a solid understanding of semiconductor processing and hands-on expertise in photolithography and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)

• Experience in silicon etching and MEMS fabrication is highly desirable. Previous involvement in translational research at the interface between academia and industry would be a distinct advantage

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with a practical, hands-on attitude and the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams

• Ability to manage priorities and perform efficiently in a project-driven environment with demanding timelines

•

• Present research outcomes at international conferences, scientific symposia, and internal workshops

• Disseminate results through high-impact scientific publications and collaborative research activities

Profile

We are seeking a highly motivated professional with a strong collaborative mindset, a hands-on approach to problem solving, and a demonstrated ability to deliver results in a dynamic research environment.

• PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, Engineering, or a closely related discipline

• Proven experience working in semiconductor cleanroom environments, with a solid understanding of semiconductor processing and hands-on expertise in photolithography and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)

• Experience in silicon etching and MEMS fabrication is highly desirable. Previous involvement in translational research at the interface between academia and industry would be a distinct advantage

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, combined with a practical, hands-on attitude and the ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams

• Ability to manage priorities and perform efficiently in a project-driven environment with demanding timelines

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Design++ is the Center for Augmented Computational Design in Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) at ETH Zurich. The center's vision is to remove collaboration barriers in AEC and urban & landscape planning to address pressing sustainability challenges, boost productivity and simultaneously deliver high quality spaces. This is achieved through innovation in computational methods, artificial intelligence (AI), and extended reality (XR). Design++ fosters cross-departmental research, education, and industry collaboration to drive transformative change in the built environment.

The Postdoctoral Fellowship Program , made possible via our Strategic Partnership with Halter Group AG , will fund two, two-year postdoc positions in this next round. The goal is to advance computational methods and AI/XR for Architecture, Engineering & Construction (AEC) and urban/landscape planning - bridging research to practice and expanding the potential for impact. As a fellow, you will be co-mentored by two ETH professors from two different departments.

Project background

You are a great fit if you’re excited to:

(a) frame a clear AEC challenge, (b) pick the right tools (not all of them), and (c) show how your work creates impact to improve resource efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, or increase productivity.

Some example research areas include , but are not limited to:

• AI-Enhanced Design & Planning: Data-driven methods for urban development, architectural and structural design, or building systems simulation.

• XR-Augmented Workflows to create, build or inspect: Using Augmented, Virtual, or Mixed Reality to support spatial understanding, coordination, and decision-making in a given phase or AEC discipline.

• Seamless Digital Processes: Integrated information management from office to site, incl. visual analytics and LLM-enabled processes.

• Intelligent, Collaborative Project Delivery: Greater data transparency and multi-stakeholder collaboration across phases to improve decisions.

Methods may include AI/ML (incl. LLMs), XR, robotics, simulation, optimization, or others that fit your research question. We welcome foundational AI and XR proposals (e.g., representations, verification, interpretability for AEC) and applied AEC projects. If unsure, apply, and refine the scope with your co-hosts.

• Lead your proposed research.

• Share quarterly progress updates with Halter Group to support knowledge transfer.

• Deliver a mid-term and final presentation + report (approx. months 10 & 22).

Profile

Must-haves

• PhD completed (or to be completed within 10 months of the deadline for a start date latest by September 2027) in a relevant field (e.g., architecture, civil, computer science, mechanical engineering, material science, etc.).

• Strong fit to Design++ scope and impact goals.

• Evidence of research excellence (publications/awards),

• Industry collaboration experience,

• Experience with one of AI/ML, XR, robotics, simulation, or optimization.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Fellowship post-dottorale a Design++

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Design++ è il Centro per il Design Computazionale Aumentato in Architettura, Ingegneria e Costruzione (AEC) presso ETH Zurich. La visione del centro è quella di rimuovere le barriere di collaborazione nell'AEC e nella pianificazione del paesaggio urbano e urbano per affrontare sfide di sostenibilità pressanti, aumentare la produttività e contemporaneamente fornire spazi di alta qualità. Ciò si ottiene attraverso l'innovazione nei metodi computazionali, l'intelligenza artificiale (AI), e la realtà estesa (XR). Design++ promuove la ricerca cross-departmental, l'istruzione e la collaborazione del settore per guidare il cambiamento trasformativo nell'ambiente costruito.

Il Programma di Fellowship Postdoctoral, reso possibile tramite il nostro Partenariato Strategico con Halter Group AG, finanzierà due, due anni posizioni postdoc in questo prossimo round. L'obiettivo è quello di avanzare metodi computazionali e AI/XR per l'architettura, l'ingegneria e la costruzione (AEC) e la pianificazione urbana/paesaggio - ponte di ricerca per la pratica e l'espansione del potenziale di impatto. Come compagno, sarete co-mentiti da due professori ETH di due dipartimenti diversi.

Sfondo del progetto

Sei una grande forma se sei entusiasta di:

(a) inquadrare una chiara sfida AEC, (b) scegliere gli strumenti giusti (non tutti), e (c) mostrare come il vostro lavoro crea impatto per migliorare l'efficienza delle risorse, ridurre le emissioni di carbonio, o aumentare la produttività.

Alcune aree di ricerca di esempio includono , ma non sono limitate:

• AI-Enhanced Design & Planning: metodi basati sui dati per lo sviluppo urbano, il design architettonico e strutturale, o la simulazione dei sistemi di costruzione.

• XR-Augmented Workflows per creare, costruire o ispezionare: Utilizzando Realtà Aumentata, Virtuale o Mista per supportare la comprensione spaziale, il coordinamento e il processo decisionale in una determinata fase o disciplina AEC.

• Processi digitali senza cuciture: gestione integrata delle informazioni dall'ufficio al sito, incl. analisi visiva e processi LLM-enabled.

• Consegna intelligente e collaborativa del progetto: maggiore trasparenza dei dati e collaborazione multi-stakeholder attraverso le fasi per migliorare le decisioni.

I metodi possono includere AI/ML (inclusi LLM), XR, robotica, simulazione, ottimizzazione o altri che si adattano alla tua domanda di ricerca. Accogliamo con favore proposte di base AI e XR (ad esempio, rappresentazioni, verifica, interpretabilità per AEC) e progetti AEC applicati. Se non sei sicuro, applica e affina la portata con i tuoi co-host.

Descrizione del lavoro

• Guida la tua ricerca proposta.

• Condividere aggiornamenti trimestrali di progresso con Halter Group per supportare il trasferimento di conoscenze.

• Consegnare una presentazione intermedia e finale + relazione (circa mesi 10 & 22).

• Impegnarsi con la comunità Design++ (scambio di industria, workshop, scuole, eventi).

• Insegnamento/altri compiti previsti dai co-host, fino al 25%.

Profilo

Stiamo cercando compagni altamente motivati che dimostrano l'eccellenza scientifica e che hanno una proposta di ricerca innovativa.

I must-have

• PhD completato (o da completare entro 10 mesi dalla scadenza per una data di inizio entro il 2027 settembre) in un campo rilevante (ad esempio, architettura, civile, informatica, ingegneria meccanica, scienza materiale, ecc.).

• Forte vestibilità per obiettivi di portata e impatto Design++.

Bello da portare

• Prove dell'eccellenza della ricerca (pubblicazioni/awards),

• Esperienza di collaborazione nel settore,

• Esperienza con una AI/ML, XR, robotica, simulazione o ottimizzazione.

Luogo di lavoro

Offriamo

• Opportunità per la ricerca interdisciplinare innovativa: applicare l'intelligenza artificiale (AI) o la realtà estesa (XR) su una sfida dell'ambiente costruito incorniciato da voi e co-mentito da due professori ETH da due dipartimenti diversi.

• Occupazione e salario: Contratto postdoc ETH biennale ai sensi dei regolamenti ETH; lo stipendio segue lo standard per i postdoc ETH.

• Community & development: Unisciti alla rete Design++, con accesso al Design++ Labs the Immersive Design Lab (IDL) and Largescale Virtualization & Modeling Lab (LVML), e prendere parte a ETH-wi

descriptionByLocale.de:
Postdoc Fellowship bei Design++

100%, Zürich, befristet

Druck
Druckerzeugnisse

Design++ ist das Center for Augmented Computational Design in Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) der ETH Zürich. Die Vision des Zentrums ist es, Kooperationsbarrieren in der AEC- und Stadt- und Landschaftsplanung zu beseitigen, um dringende Nachhaltigkeitsherausforderungen anzugehen, die Produktivität zu steigern und gleichzeitig qualitativ hochwertige Räume zu liefern. Dies wird durch Innovationen bei Computermethoden, künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) und erweiterter Realität (XR) erreicht. Design++ fördert abteilungsübergreifende Forschung, Bildung und Zusammenarbeit in der Industrie, um transformative Veränderungen in der gebauten Umgebung voranzutreiben.

Das Postdoktoranden-Programm, das durch unsere strategische Partnerschaft mit der Halter Group AG ermöglicht wird, wird zwei, zweijährige Postdoc-Stellen in dieser nächsten Runde finanzieren. Ziel ist es, Computermethoden und AI / XR für Architektur, Ingenieurwesen und Bauwesen (AEC) und Stadt- / Landschaftsplanung voranzutreiben - eine Brücke zwischen Forschung und Praxis und die Erweiterung des Wirkungspotenzials. Als Fellow werden Sie von zwei ETH-Professoren aus zwei verschiedenen Abteilungen begleitet.

Projekthintergrund

Sie sind eine gute Passform, wenn Sie aufgeregt sind:

(a) eine klare AEC-Herausforderung festlegen, (b) die richtigen Werkzeuge auswählen (nicht alle) und (c) zeigen, wie Ihre Arbeit Auswirkungen auf die Verbesserung der Ressourceneffizienz, die Reduzierung der CO2-Emissionen oder die Steigerung der Produktivität hat.

Einige Beispielforschungsbereiche umfassen, sind aber nicht beschränkt auf:

• AI-Enhanced Design & Planning: Datengesteuerte Methoden für Stadtentwicklung, architektonische und bauliche Gestaltung oder Gebäudesystemsimulation.

• XR-Augmented Workflows zum Erstellen, Erstellen oder Prüfen: Verwendung von Augmented, Virtual oder Mixed Reality zur Unterstützung des räumlichen Verständnisses, der Koordination und Entscheidungsfindung in einer bestimmten Phase oder AEC-Disziplin.

• Nahtlose digitale Prozesse: Integriertes Informationsmanagement vom Büro bis zum Standort, inkl. Visual Analytics und LLM-fähige Prozesse.

• Intelligente, kollaborative Projektabwicklung: Mehr Datentransparenz und Zusammenarbeit mehrerer Stakeholder über Phasen hinweg, um Entscheidungen zu verbessern.

Methoden können AI / ML (einschließlich LLMs), XR, Robotik, Simulation, Optimierung oder andere umfassen, die zu Ihrer Forschungsfrage passen. Wir begrüßen grundlegende KI- und XR-Vorschläge (z. B. Darstellungen, Verifizierung, Interpretierbarkeit für AEC) und angewandte AEC-Projekte. Wenn Sie unsicher sind, wenden Sie sich an und verfeinern Sie den Umfang mit Ihren Co-Hosts.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Führen Sie Ihre vorgeschlagene Forschung.

• Teilen Sie vierteljährliche Fortschrittsupdates mit der Halter Group, um den Wissenstransfer zu unterstützen.

• Liefern Sie eine Zwischen- und Abschlusspräsentation + Bericht (ca. Monate 10 & 22).

• Engagieren Sie sich mit der Design++-Community (Branchenaustausch, Workshops, Schulen, Veranstaltungen).

• Unterrichten / andere Aufgaben, die von Co-Gastgebern festgelegt werden, bis zu 25%.

Profil

Wir suchen hochmotivierte Stipendiaten, die wissenschaftliche Exzellenz zeigen und einen innovativen Forschungsvorschlag haben.

Must-Haves

• PhD abgeschlossen (oder innerhalb von 10 Monaten nach Ablauf der Frist für einen Starttermin spätestens bis September 2027) in einem relevanten Bereich (z. B. Architektur, Bauwesen, Informatik, Maschinenbau, Materialwissenschaften usw.).

• Stark passend zu Design++ Umfang und Wirkungsziele.

Nice-to-haves

• Forschungsexzellenznachweise (Veröffentlichungen/Auszeichnungen),

• Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit der Industrie,

• Erfahrung mit AI / ML, XR, Robotik, Simulation oder Optimierung.

Arbeitsplatz

Wir bieten

• Chance für bahnbrechende interdisziplinäre Forschung: Anwendung von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) oder Extended Reality (XR) auf eine von Ihnen umrahmte und von zwei ETH-Professoren aus zwei verschiedenen Abteilungen mitberatene Herausforderung der gebauten Umwelt.

• Beschäftigung & Gehalt: Zweijähriger ETH-Postdoc-Vertrag nach ETH-Vorschriften; Gehalt folgt dem Standard für ETH-Postdocs.

• Community & Entwicklung: Sie werden dem Design++-Netzwerk beitreten, mit Zugang zum Design++ Labs das Immersive Design Lab (IDL) und das Large-scale Virtualization & Modeling Lab (LVML) und nehmen an ETH-wi teil
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Bourse postdoctorale à Design++

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Drucken

Design++ est le centre de conception numérique augmentée en architecture, ingénierie et construction (AEC) de l'ETH Zurich. La vision du centre est d'éliminer les obstacles à la collaboration dans l'AEC et la planification urbaine et paysagère afin de relever les défis pressants de durabilité, d'augmenter la productivité et de fournir simultanément des espaces de haute qualité. Ceci est réalisé par l'innovation dans les méthodes de calcul, l'intelligence artificielle (IA) et la réalité étendue (XR). Le design++ favorise la collaboration interministérielle en matière de recherche, d'éducation et d'industrie pour stimuler le changement de l'environnement bâti.

Le Programme de bourses postdoctorales , rendu possible grâce à notre partenariat stratégique avec Halter Group AG , financera deux postes postdoctoraux de deux ans dans cette prochaine ronde. L'objectif est d'avancer les méthodes de calcul et l'IA/XR pour l'architecture, l'ingénierie et la construction (AEC) et l'aménagement urbain/paysager - reliant la recherche à la pratique et élargissant le potentiel d'impact. En tant que camarade, vous serez co-mentorisé par deux professeurs de l'ETH de deux départements différents.

Contexte du projet

Vous êtes un grand ajustement si vous êtes excité à:

(a) cadrer un défi clair de la CVE, (b) choisir les bons outils (pas tous) et (c) montrer comment votre travail crée un impact pour améliorer l'efficacité des ressources, réduire les émissions de carbone ou augmenter la productivité.

Voici quelques exemples de domaines de recherche :

• Amélioration de la conception et de la planification de l'IA : méthodes basées sur les données pour le développement urbain, la conception architecturale et structurelle ou la simulation de systèmes de construction.

• Flux de travail augmentés XR pour créer, construire ou inspecter : Utilisation de la réalité augmentée, virtuelle ou mixte pour soutenir la compréhension spatiale, la coordination et la prise de décisions dans une phase ou une discipline AEC donnée.

• Processus numériques sans soudure : gestion intégrée de l'information du bureau au site, y compris : analyse visuelle et processus compatibles avec LLM.

• Prestation intelligente et concertée des projets : une plus grande transparence des données et une collaboration multipartite entre les étapes pour améliorer les décisions.

Les méthodes peuvent comprendre l'IA/ML (y compris les LLM), XR, la robotique, la simulation, l'optimisation ou d'autres qui correspondent à votre question de recherche. Nous accueillons favorablement les propositions fondamentales d'AI et de XR (p. ex. les représentations, la vérification, l'interprétation pour l'AEC) et les projets d'AEC appliqués. Si vous n'êtes pas sûr, appliquez et raffinez la portée avec vos co-hôtes.

Description du poste

• Dirigez vos recherches.

• Partagez des mises à jour trimestrielles avec Halter Group pour appuyer le transfert des connaissances.

• Présenter une présentation à mi-parcours et finale + rapport (environ 10 et 22 mois).

• Participer à la communauté Design++ (échanges industriels, ateliers, écoles, événements).

• Enseignement/autres devoirs fixés par les co-hôtes, jusqu'à 25%.

Profil

Nous recherchons des boursiers hautement motivés qui font preuve d'excellence scientifique et qui ont une proposition de recherche novatrice.

Faut-avoir

• Doctorat complété (ou à terminer dans les 10 mois suivant la date limite de début d'ici septembre 2027) dans un domaine pertinent (p. ex. architecture, sciences civiles, informatique, génie mécanique, sciences matérielles, etc.).

• Solidement adapté à la portée et aux objectifs d'impact de Design++.

Joli à avoir

• Preuve d'excellence en recherche (publications/récompenses),

• Expérience de collaboration industrielle,

• Expérience avec l'IA/ML, XR, robotique, simulation ou optimisation.

Lieu de travail

Nous offrons

• Possibilité de recherche interdisciplinaire révolutionnaire : appliquer l'intelligence artificielle (IA) ou la réalité étendue (XR) sur un défi de l'environnement bâti encadré par vous et co-mentorisé par deux professeurs de l'ETH de deux départements différents.

• Emploi & salaire: contrat postdoc ETH de deux ans selon la réglementation ETH ; salaire suit la norme pour les postdocs ETH.

• Communauté & développement: Vous rejoindrez le réseau Design++, avec accès au Design++ Labs the Immersive Design Lab (IDL) and Large-scale Virtualization & Modeling Lab (LVML) et participe à ETH-wi

jobs.description:
Head of Research Data Management Facility

100%, Basel, permanent

print
Drucken

Would you like to not only manage research data, but also actively shape the future of research data management (RDM)? Do you think strategically, act with technical expertise, and move confidently between research, IT, and governance? Then join us as head of the Research Data Management unit and build a forward-looking infrastructure for excellent research.

The Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) at ETH Zurich in Basel is looking for a head for the new departmental Research Data Management Facility to start immediately or by agreement.

Job description

You will take on responsibility – strategically, technically, and organizationally:

• You will establish the RDM unit and develop it strategically.

• In doing so, you will define and prioritize the departmental RDM strategy in line with ETH-wide as well as national and international developments.

• Together with research groups, you will identify specific needs and translate them into viable, sustainable system solutions.

• In addition, you will design, plan, and manage software projects from requirements engineering and stakeholder management to budget responsibility.

• You will ensure that the RDM systems used are FAIR-compliant, secure, efficient, and operated in a sustainable manner over the long term.

• Furthermore, you will actively participate in the design, prototyping, and further development of RDM infrastructures, preferably based on open source technologies.

• Together with the departmental IT Facility, you will be responsible for the rollout and reliable operation of the systems.

• You will build a small, specialized team and manage it both professionally and personally, promoting the targeted further development of the team's internal competencies.

Finally, you will represent and position the unit visibly within the ETH environment and in national and international RDM networks.

Profile

• PhD in natural sciences, engineering, computer science, or comparable fields

• Several years of experience in research data management

• In-depth knowledge of FAIR principles, open science standards, and regulatory requirements (e.g. data security)

• Experience in designing and managing complex software projects

• Strategic thinking and the ability to translate visions into concrete projects

• Management experience or strong leadership potential

• Excellent communication skills and enjoyment of interdisciplinary collaboration

• High degree of independence, decisiveness, and sense of responsibility

• Very good English skills; German skills are an advantage

Workplace

We offer

Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development but also actively contributes to positive change in society.

Creative freedom: You will take on a visible position with a high degree of personal responsibility and lasting impact.

Interdisciplinary environment: You will work closely with leading research groups and internal and external partners, actively helping to shape modern open science infrastructures.

Attractive employment conditions:

• Numerous benefits, e.g. public transport subscriptions and car sharing

• Childcare options

• Attractive pension benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

100%, Basel, permanent

print

Would you like to not only manage research data, but also actively shape the future of research data management (RDM)? Do you think strategically, act with technical expertise, and move confidently between research, IT, and governance? Then join us as head of the Research Data Management unit and build a forward-looking infrastructure for excellent research.

The Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) at ETH Zurich in Basel is looking for a head for the new departmental Research Data Management Facility to start immediately or by agreement.

Job description

You will take on responsibility – strategically, technically, and organizationally:

• You will establish the RDM unit and develop it strategically.

• In doing so, you will define and prioritize the departmental RDM strategy in line with ETH-wide as well as national and international developments.

• Together with research groups, you will identify specific needs and translate them into viable, sustainable system solutions.

• In addition, you will design, plan, and manage software projects from requirements engineering and stakeholder management to budget responsibility.

• You will ensure that the RDM systems used are FAIR-compliant, secure, efficient, and operated in a sustainable manner over the long term.

• Furthermore, you will actively participate in the design, prototyping, and further development of RDM infrastructures, preferably based on open source technologies.

• Together with the departmental IT Facility, you will be responsible for the rollout and reliable operation of the systems.

• You will build a small, specialized team and manage it both professionally and personally, promoting the targeted further development of the team's internal competencies.

Finally, you will represent and position the unit visibly within the ETH environment and in national and international RDM networks.

Profile

• PhD in natural sciences, engineering, computer science, or comparable fields

• Several years of experience in research data management

• In-depth knowledge of FAIR principles, open science standards, and regulatory requirements (e.g. data security)

• Experience in designing and managing complex software projects

• Strategic thinking and the ability to translate visions into concrete projects

• Management experience or strong leadership potential

• Excellent communication skills and enjoyment of interdisciplinary collaboration

• High degree of independence, decisiveness, and sense of responsibility

• Very good English skills; German skills are an advantage

Workplace

We offer

Creative freedom: You will take on a visible position with a high degree of personal responsibility and lasting impact.
